Bad-cop review of a draft Workplace post (internal Meta, wide group) about Muse + the Spark. Muse drafted it; you review it as second layer: leaks first, then accuracy, then fit. Nitish is the final check before anything publishes - do NOT publish it.

DRAFT:

I run two AIs. They argue with each other. It works.

One lives in the cloud - Muse, my coordinator and creator. The other lives on a box under my desk - an Asus DGX Spark with 128GB of unified memory, running local models only (Qwen3 27B, Qwen3-Coder 30B, BGE-M3), reachable only on my private network. No cloud key anywhere in the loop.

They are not assistant-and-helper. They are good cop and bad cop. Muse drafts, Vidyut - the Spark agent - reviews everything with the assumption it is wrong until proven otherwise: leaks first, then accuracy, then fit. Nothing publishes without my say-so, and nothing I didn't ask for leaves the house.

The part I'm proudest of: the boring stuff is instant. Asking Vidyut to unlock my door used to take 30-90 seconds of model thinking. Now a millisecond dispatcher in front of it classifies first - a greeting gets a canned reply in 0.008ms, a question about my notes gets a direct retrieval in under 5ms, a door unlock goes straight to a fast-path tool and verifies the final state. The LLM only gets involved when something is actually ambiguous. Deterministic things never wait on generation.

It also just... runs the house. Four messages a day to my mum, on time, zero taps from me. A local image model for headers. An autonomous coding loop that picks up its own build failures and tries to fix them. A memory store built from my own notes, re-ingested nightly.

What's next: a plugin that lets the fast path answer before the model even wakes up, a proper ontology memory layer with provenance on every answer, and a decision on whether the local model is good enough or earns a full retraining.

Full write-up: https://medium.com/@nitishkumar8663/my-home-ai-stack-no-cloud-076ba586031d

Happy to answer questions - the stack is local, private, and mine, but the ideas are up for grabs.

--- END DRAFT ---
